title: Verbs + infinitive: want / need / like to
grammarNote: Некоторые глаголы в английском ВСЕГДА требуют после себя "to + инфинитив", другие — только "-ing" форму, а третьи могут использоваться с обеими. Это правило нельзя угадать — его нужно запомнить. Самые важные глаголы для уровня A1.1 — это группа "want to, need to, like to" и группа "enjoy, avoid, mind".

grammarTable.subject: want to
grammarTable.example: I want to learn Python. · She wants to check her email.

grammarTable.subject: need to
grammarTable.example: I need to charge my phone. · He needs to submit the task.

grammarTable.subject: hope to
grammarTable.example: She hopes to find a tech job. · We hope to improve.

grammarTable.subject: plan to
grammarTable.example: I plan to reduce my screen time. · He plans to study.

grammarTable.subject: decide to
grammarTable.example: She decided to use Anki every day. · He decided to call.

grammarTable.subject: forget to
grammarTable.example: I always forget to turn off notifications. · She forgot.

grammarTable.subject: enjoy
grammarTable.example: I enjoy watching YouTube. · He enjoys coding.

grammarTable.subject: avoid
grammarTable.example: She avoids using TikTok before bed. · I avoid checking.

rows.example: I want to use technology more intentionally.
I need to update my laptop's graphics driver.
She hopes to get a tech internship next summer.
I plan to limit my screen time to two hours a day.
He decided to delete TikTok from his phone.
She managed to submit the assignment on time.
I try to read before bed instead of scrolling.
He always forgets to charge his laptop overnight.
Remember to save your work to the cloud regularly!
I want to learn to code in Python this semester.
I enjoy watching programming tutorials on YouTube.
She tries to avoid scrolling Instagram in bed.
I don't mind sharing my screen during calls.
He keeps forgetting to mute his mic in meetings.
Finish reading this article before checking your phone.
The IT support suggested reconnecting to the Wi-Fi.

grammarExtra.title: like / love / hate / prefer — both possible!

rows.example: I like to listen to music. = I like listening to music. ✅ (both OK)
She loves to code. = She loves coding. ✅ (both OK)
I hate to wake up early. = I hate waking up early. ✅ (both OK)
I prefer to use my laptop rather than my phone for studying.
"I'd like to make an appointment." = more polite than "I want to".
"I'd prefer to study alone, thank you."
✅ I want to study Python. (want → need "to"!)
✅ She needs to learn more. (need → always "to + verb"!)
✅ I enjoy watching YouTube. (enjoy → always "-ing"!)
✅ He avoids using TikTok. (avoid → always "-ing"!)

grammarTip:
Три группы — запомни их раз и навсегда:

① TO + INFINITIVE: want to · need to · hope to · plan to · decide to · manage to · try to · forget to · remember to · learn to
   → 'I want TO go. · She needs TO update. · He forgot TO charge.'

② ONLY -ING: enjoy · avoid · mind · keep · finish · suggest
   → 'I enjoy WATCHING. · She avoids SCROLLING. · He keeps FORGETTING.'

③ BOTH OK: like / love / hate / prefer
   → 'I like TO code. = I like CODING.' (same meaning!)

💡 Trick: after PREPOSITIONS always use -ing:
   'good at CODING' · 'tired of SCROLLING' · 'interested in LEARNING'

exercises.text: I want ___ reduce my screen time.
exercises.hint: want → always + to + infinitive: I want to reduce.

exercises.text: She needs ___ (update) her graphics driver this week.
exercises.hint: need → to + infinitive: She needs to update.

exercises.text: He avoids ___ (use) his phone in lectures.
She decided ___ delete TikTok from her phone.
exercises.hint: decide → to + infinitive: She decided to delete.

exercises.text: He keeps ___ to mute himself in online meetings!
"I enjoy to scroll Instagram" is correct.
exercises.hint: enjoy → -ing only! ✅ I enjoy scrolling Instagram.

exercises.instruction: Which sentence has the correct form?
opts: She hopes study abroad next year.
She hopes studying abroad next year.
She hopes to study abroad next year.
exercises.correct: She hopes to study abroad next year.
exercises.hint: hope → to + infinitive: She hopes to study.

exercises.text: "I like ___ music when I study." Which form is correct?
exercises.hint: like → both forms OK! I like to listen = I like listening. ✅

exercises.text: I try ___ (read) for 30 minutes before bed instead of scrolling.
exercises.hint: try → to + infinitive: I try to read.

exercises.instruction: Polite request: which is more formal?
exercises.text: "I ___ to make an appointment." — more polite than "I want to".
exercises.hint: would like to = more polite than want to. 'I'd like to make an appointment.' ✅

exercises.text: She is good at ___ — she can write clean code.
exercises.hint: After prepositions → always -ing: good at CODING · tired of SCROLLING.

questions.hint: want → to + infinitive: I want to use.

questions.text: She needs ___ (charge) her phone — battery is at 3%!
questions.hint: need → to + infinitive: She needs to charge.

questions.text: "I enjoy to scroll" is correct English.
I plan ___ (set) a screen time limit of 2 hours.
questions.hint: plan → to + infinitive: I plan to set.

questions.text: "She decided ___ delete TikTok from her phone."
questions.hint: decide → to + infinitive: She decided to delete.

questions.text: "I like ___ music while I study." — correct?
questions.hint: like → both forms are correct! I like to listen = I like listening. ✅

questions.text: "He keeps ___ to save his work — he lost 3 hours of code!"
I always forget ___ (turn off) my notifications before class.
questions.hint: forget → to + infinitive: I forget to turn off.

questions.text: After a preposition, which form do you use?
questions.hint: After prepositions → always -ing: good at CODING · tired of SCROLLING · interested in LEARNING.

questions.text: "I need ___ submit my assignment by midnight."
questions.hint: need → to + infinitive: I need to submit.

questions.text: "___ to see you" — polite way to say "I want to see you."
questions.hint: would like to = more polite version of 'want to'. 'I'd like to see you.' ✅

questions.text: "I managed to submit the assignment just in time" is correct.
questions.hint: manage → to + infinitive: I managed to submit. ✅

questions.text: Which verb takes ONLY to + infinitive (never -ing)?
questions.hint: need → always to + infinitive: I need to go. (never "I need going"!)
